name: Snap
description: Snap is a classic children's card game that tests mental reaction speed and pattern recognition. Players take turns flipping cards from their personal piles onto a central pile or their own discard pile. When two cards of the same rank (e.g., two 7s) appear consecutively or simultaneously on top of piles, the first player to shout 'Snap!' wins the cards. The goal is to win the entire deck.

content.text: Snap is a classic children's card game that tests mental reaction speed and pattern recognition. Players take turns flipping cards from their personal piles onto a central pile or their own discard pile. When two cards of the same rank (e.g., two 7s) appear consecutively or simultaneously on top of piles, the first player to shout 'Snap!' wins the cards. The goal is to win the entire deck.
Dates back to the Victorian era (1866 recorded rules). Originally called 'Wait a Minute' or similar names.
Two to four players typically; the game can be played by up to about six, beyond which it becomes unwieldy. Each player keeps their cards in a face-down stack in front of them.
A standard 52-card pack is used. Suits do not matter; only the ranks (A, 2–10, J, Q, K) matter for matching. Some play with special Snap or matching-card packs.

items.text: Single Pile: Players turn cards onto a single central pile. When two consecutive cards match, any player may call Snap and the first to do so wins the centre pile. A player who calls Snap incorrectly gives the top card of their pile to the player who turned the card. Simultaneous calls create a snap pool; first to call Snap pool when the centre matches a pool wins the pool.

Simultaneous calls: If two or more players shout Snap at the same time, the matching piles are combined into a snap pool in the centre. If two or more call Snap pool simultaneously, the matching player pile is added to that pool. Some groups use an object in the centre to grab; the hand underneath on the object decides who was first.
